cues.en: YouTube was kind enough to publish their deep learning architecture, at least as it was in 2016.
cues.zh: YouTube 很大方地公布了深度學習架構，至少是 2016 年的版本。

cues.en: Let's start at the bottom, where we have the user behavior data that is used to train the system.
cues.zh: 從底部開始，這是訓練系統所用的使用者行為資料。

cues.en: It's interesting that although YouTube has explicit ratings in the form of thumbs up/thumbs down ratings, they don't use them at all for generating recommendations, because that data is too sparse.
cues.zh: 有趣的是，雖然 YouTube 有按讚、倒讚這類明確評分，但完全不用它們產生推薦，因為資料太稀疏。

cues.en: Not enough users rate videos explicitly for the data to be useful.
cues.zh: 明確評分的使用者不夠多，資料不足以派上用場。

cues.en: Instead, they rely on implicit signals, such as which videos you actually watched, and what you searched for.
cues.zh: 他們改依賴隱含訊號，例如你實際看過哪些影片，以及搜尋過什麼。

cues.en: This implicit view and search data, however, is in itself sparse, and as we learned when covering deep learning recommenders, dealing with that sparsity is a huge issue
cues.zh: 不過，這些隱含觀看與搜尋資料本身也很稀疏。介紹深度學習推薦器時已經學過，處理這種稀疏性，是很大的問題，

cues.en: when trying to apply deep learning to recommender systems.
cues.zh: 尤其在把深度學習應用於推薦系統時。

cues.en: Their solution was to break up the sparse representation of video IDs and search tokens for each user, into a variable-length sequence of sparse data, mapped to a dense layer of a fixed length,
cues.zh: 解法是把每位使用者的影片 ID 與搜尋詞元的稀疏表示，拆成可變長度的稀疏資料序列，再映射到固定長度的密集層，

cues.en: suitable for input to a neural network in an embedding layer.
cues.zh: 作為嵌入層中適合輸入神經網路的資料。

cues.en: They simply average each chunk of the sparse input data.
cues.zh: 他們直接對稀疏輸入資料的每個區塊取平均。

cues.en: To say it another way, they split up each user's sparse behavior data into chunks of a fixed length, and take the average of each chunk, to reduce that data into fixed-length embedding layer,
cues.zh: 換句話說，把每位使用者的稀疏行為資料切成固定長度區塊，對每個區塊取平均，將資料縮減為固定長度的嵌入層，

cues.en: that can be used as input to their neural network.
cues.zh: 作為神經網路的輸入。

cues.en: They restrict this embedding to the most popular videos or search terms in order to keep it manageable for the scale they are dealing with.
cues.zh: 他們只對最熱門的影片或搜尋詞建立這種嵌入，才能在所需規模下保持可管理性。

cues.en: Any obscure video you watch, ends up getting mapped to the value zero.
cues.zh: 你看的任何冷門影片，最後都會映射成 0。

cues.en: This may seem like an arbitrary choice, but they experimented with other ways of doing it, including summing and taking the max value for each component.
cues.zh: 這看似任意選擇，但他們也實驗過其他方式，包括對各成分加總或取最大值。

cues.en: And the way the embeddings work is itself learned through gradient descent backpropagation, so their system is actually learning the best way to reduce the dimensionality of their sparse data.
cues.zh: 嵌入的運作方式本身，也透過梯度下降與反向傳播學習，所以系統其實在學習，如何最好地降低稀疏資料的維度。

cues.en: In this way, they've avoided the problem of only training the system on videos or search tokens that were actually invoked by any individual user.
cues.zh: 如此就避免了只使用個別使用者實際接觸過的影片或搜尋詞元來訓練系統的問題。

cues.en: At the next layer, they combine together those averaged video watch vectors and search token vectors, with any other training features they want to incorporate into their model, such as the user's geographic location,
cues.zh: 下一層，把這些平均後的影片觀看向量與搜尋詞元向量，和其他想納入模型的訓練特徵合併，例如使用者的地理位置，

cues.en: their age, their gender, and presumably other features not shown here.
cues.zh: 年齡、性別，以及這裡可能沒顯示的其他特徵。

cues.en: All of those concatenated features are then fed as input into a deep neural network, trained with softmax.
cues.zh: 所有串接的特徵，接著作為輸入，送入以 softmax 訓練的深度神經網路。

cues.en: They settled on three layers.
cues.zh: 最後採用三層。

cues.en: The first has a width of 1,024 units, followed by 512, and then 256 at the top.
cues.zh: 第一層寬度為 1,024 個單元，接著是 512，最上層是 256。

cues.en: This gave them a good balance of accuracy, while staying within their budget for computing hardware.
cues.zh: 這讓準確度與運算硬體預算之間取得良好平衡。

cues.en: The output of all this is fed into a database of nearest neighbors for each video, to generate more recommendation candidates, based on what the deep neural network found.
cues.zh: 這些輸出會送入每部影片的最近鄰資料庫，根據深度神經網路找到的結果，產生更多候選推薦。

cues.en: The problem is then to optimally rank all of these candidates.
cues.zh: 接著的問題，是如何最佳排列所有候選項目。

cues.en: Given their mandate to use deep learning for everything, YouTube also uses deep learning to rank their recommendation candidates to produce a final top-N set of recommendations.
cues.zh: 因為要求所有事情都用深度學習，YouTube 也用深度學習排列候選推薦，產生最終 Top-N 推薦集合。

cues.en: This isn't a new idea, it's called learning to rank, and there's a fair amount of research behind it as well.
cues.zh: 這不是新想法，叫做學習排序，背後也有相當多研究。

cues.en: They throw as many features into this neural network as they can.
cues.zh: 他們盡可能把各種特徵送入這個神經網路。

cues.en: They take the entire impression history for the user, that is, every video that was showed to them, prior to viewing the video that generated this recommendation.
cues.zh: 他們取出使用者完整的曝光紀錄，也就是在觀看引發這次推薦的影片之前，曾顯示給他的每部影片。

cues.en: These are embedded and averaged in a similar way to how the sparse view data was encoded to generate recommendation candidates.
cues.zh: 這些資料也做嵌入並取平均，方式類似產生候選推薦時，對稀疏觀看資料進行編碼的做法。

cues.en: The language of the user and the language of the video are also embedded into another feature set.
cues.zh: 使用者的語言與影片的語言，也嵌入到另一組特徵。

cues.en: They also look at the time elapsed since the user last watched a video on this topic.
cues.zh: 他們也看使用者上次觀看這個主題影片，到現在經過多久。

cues.en: And they look at the number of previous impressions this user had, which is actually used as a training feature in several different ways.
cues.zh: 還看使用者之前的曝光次數，這其實以幾種不同方式作為訓練特徵。

cues.en: They take the square root of this value, the square of it, and the value itself, all as separate input features.
cues.zh: 取這個值的平方根、平方，以及值本身，全部作為獨立輸入特徵。

cues.en: This allows the system to discover super and sublinear functions, which is a neat trick.
cues.zh: 這讓系統能發現超線性與次線性函數，是個很巧妙的技巧。

cues.en: Everything is normalized before being fed into the neural network, of course, to make all of these features have equal initial weight.
cues.zh: 當然，所有資料送入神經網路前都會正規化，讓這些特徵具有相同的初始權重。

cues.en: The output of all this is actually used to predict the expected watch time of each video, which is ultimately what the ranking depends on.
cues.zh: 整體輸出其實用來預測每部影片的預期觀看時間，而排序最終就依據這個值。

cues.en: They don't want to optimize on predicting just clicks on a video, because this tends to surface clickbait videos that people aren't actually interested in.
cues.zh: 他們不想只最佳化影片點擊預測，因為這往往會凸顯人們其實不感興趣的釣魚標題影片。

cues.en: If a user actually watches a video all the way through, however, that's a stronger indication of it satisfying that individual's interests.
cues.zh: 但如果使用者真的從頭到尾看完，就更能顯示影片符合他的興趣。

cues.en: This is an important point.
cues.zh: 這點很重要。

cues.en: YouTube is optimizing for minutes watched, not for clicks.
cues.zh: YouTube 最佳化的是觀看分鐘數，而非點擊。

cues.en: And this decision alone has motivated professional YouTubers to upload longer and longer videos, in an effort to increase that watch-time metric.
cues.zh: 光是這個決定，就驅使職業 YouTuber 上傳越來越長的影片，試圖增加觀看時間指標。

cues.en: They've sort of inadvertently introduced a new way to game the system.
cues.zh: 他們有點像無意間引入了操弄系統的新方法。

cues.en: They also refine the actual objective function they use to produce those final results through continual A/B testing, to try and find the function that best maximizes minutes watched.
cues.zh: 他們也透過持續 A/B 測試，改進產生最終結果所用的實際目標函數，嘗試找出最能提高觀看分鐘數的函數。

cues.en: I think it's interesting that the need to combat the noisiness of video click data with minutes watched data, has led to YouTube building a system that tries to drive watch time over all else.
cues.zh: 我覺得很有趣：為了用觀看分鐘數對抗影片點擊資料的雜訊，YouTube 最後建立了一個把觀看時間放在一切之上的系統。

cues.en: Fighting that noise has resulted in people spending more and more time on YouTube, and YouTube spending more and more resources to deliver all that video content.
cues.zh: 對抗雜訊的結果，是人們在 YouTube 花越來越多時間，YouTube 也花越來越多資源傳送所有影片內容。

cues.en: It's an example of a recommender system having consequences that are perhaps unintended.
cues.zh: 這是推薦系統可能產生非預期後果的例子。

cues.en: Here are some key takeaways from the paper as a whole.
cues.zh: 以下是整篇論文的幾個重點。

cues.en: First, don't rely on just view data when training a recommender system.
cues.zh: 首先，訓練推薦系統時，不要只依賴觀看資料。

cues.en: The folks at YouTube came up with as many signals as they could from the user's past behavior and the user's attributes, and for some features, they also fed these in as squares and square roots,
cues.zh: YouTube 團隊從使用者過去行為與屬性，盡可能找出各種訊號；有些特徵，也會送入其平方與平方根，

cues.en: in case there were nonlinear relationships to be found.
cues.zh: 以便發現可能存在的非線性關係。

cues.en: View data alone is too easily gamed, and rewards clickbait videos that don't actually reflect a user's interests.
cues.zh: 單靠觀看資料太容易被操弄，也會獎勵並不真正反映使用者興趣的釣魚標題影片。

cues.en: They also withhold some information from their recommender system in order to prevent overfitting.
cues.zh: 他們也刻意不讓推薦系統取得某些資訊，以避免過度擬合。

cues.en: For example, predicting a user will watch a Taylor Swift music video just because they searched for Taylor Swift, isn't really helpful.
cues.zh: 例如，只因使用者搜尋 Taylor Swift，就預測他會看 Taylor Swift 的音樂影片，其實沒什麼幫助。

cues.en: They would've found that video anyhow from the search results, and the relationship between that search and that video is a little too direct.
cues.zh: 反正使用者也會從搜尋結果找到那部影片，而且搜尋與影片之間的關係太直接。

cues.en: As a result, they discard sequence information, and obscure the search data fed into their system to try and prevent this sort of overfitting.
cues.zh: 因此，他們捨棄順序資訊，並模糊送入系統的搜尋資料，嘗試避免這類過度擬合。

cues.en: It's very common for YouTube users to watch videos that are part of a series.
cues.zh: YouTube 使用者很常觀看同一系列的影片。

cues.en: An episodic series of videos will generally be watched in order.
cues.zh: 分集的影片系列，通常會依序觀看。

cues.en: So they need to try and predict specifically the next video a user will watch, and not some randomly held-out future view.
cues.zh: 所以必須具體預測使用者接著會看的影片，而非隨機保留的某次未來觀看。

cues.en: This means that leave-one-out cross validation as we've shown earlier in the course, doesn't meet their needs.
cues.zh: 這表示先前課程示範的留一法交叉驗證，無法滿足他們的需求。

cues.en: They aren't trying to predict a randomly held-out view, they must focus specifically on the next view.
cues.zh: 他們不是要預測隨機保留的觀看，而必須特別聚焦下一次觀看。

cues.en: But the main takeaway is that they are ranking by actual consumption, minutes watched, and not just clicks on videos.
cues.zh: 不過最主要的重點，是他們依實際使用情況，也就是觀看分鐘數排序，而非只看影片點擊。

cues.en: Clickstream data is fraught with peril, and they've learned this the hard way.
cues.zh: 點擊流資料充滿風險，他們也是付出代價才學到。

cues.en: Another important thing you've learned is that you can apply machine learning not only to generating recommendation candidates, but also to how these candidates are ranked.
cues.zh: 另一個重要收穫是，機器學習不只能用來產生候選推薦，也能用來決定如何排列候選項目。

cues.en: The systems we've covered in this course produce some sort of final recommendation score for each candidate that you can sort to produce top-N recommendations.
cues.zh: 本課程介紹的系統，會為每個候選項目產生某種最終推薦分數，排序後就能得到 Top-N 推薦。

cues.en: But sometimes there is additional information you can incorporate into that ranking.
cues.zh: 但有時還有其他資訊，可以納入排序。

cues.en: And how that information is applied, can itself be learned.
cues.zh: 而如何運用這些資訊，本身也能透過學習決定。
